extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent administrators, patent attorneys, agents, and KIPO/IPTAB examiners handling representation and powers of attorney in Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements governing who may represent parties in patent-/utility-model-/design-/trademark-related proceedings before the Korean Intellectual Property Office and related courts, what powers/authorities are required, how powers are proved/registered, and how replacements/sub-agents operate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirement for patent attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Only registered (qualified) patent attorneys may carry out proceedings as a patent attorney before the Korean Intellectual Property Office or courts; an unregistered patent attorney cannot conduct such proceedings and should be punished if they have conducted business as a patent attorney. A person who is not a patent attorney shall not use the title of patent attorney or similar titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict prohibition: representation before KIPO/courts requires registration; misuse of title is forbidden and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest / prior-representation prohibition (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent attorney shall not handle a case which he has previously handled as a representative of the other party in the same case (i.e., may not represent the opposing party in the same matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation is treated as deficiencies in the power of attorney; examiner may order amendment under Article 46 and invalidate proceedings if deficiencies are not addressed. Note example and Supreme Court case indicating application to the same case context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal representative defined and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal representative is a representative empowered by legal provisions (not by principal’s intention); the system protects persons incapable of carrying out lawsuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal representatives' authority is broad; appointment may be by law or by court recognition; legal representative status affects rights (e.g., right to appoint subagents) and extinguishment rules per Civil Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation/change/extinguishment of legal representation (Civil Act rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generation, change and extinguishment of authority for legal representation shall be made according to the Civil Act. Grounds for extinguishment include death of the principal or legal representative, adjudication of incompetency or bankruptcy of legal representative, and resignation/removal of guardian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent-related proceedings are interrupted when a legal representative dies or loses authority. Effects of extinguishment/change are not claimed against counterparties unless notified per Civil Procedure Act examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different scopes for parent (person with parental authority) vs guardian
rubrics_metrics.description: A person with parental authority can conduct any patent-related proceedings (including trial or retrial) without consent of a guardian supervisor; a guardian is more restricted and must obtain guardian supervisor consent for acts relating to acquisition, forfeit or alteration of patent rights and for filing petitions for trial/retrial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Civil Act note: guardian has restricted authority for specified significant acts (borrowing, imposing obligations, bringing actions, handling important property etc.); evidential documents of consent required where guardian acts outside default scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required when legal representative acts
rubrics_metrics.description: When a legal representative conducts a patent-related proceeding, they must state such facts in the ‘Agent’ box on application cover sheets and submit evidential documents (e.g., certified copy of resident registration or family relations certificates for parents; evidential documents and guardian supervisor consent where required for guardians).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner can confirm status via resident registration database, submission of evidential documents may not be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual representative: creation and extinguishment of authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractual representative receives credential from a principal and becomes a representative according to the principal's intention; power of representation is generated when principal grants power of attorney and extinguished when the principal withdraws the empowering authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Act modifies typical Civil Act lapse causes: power of representation may survive death or loss of legal capacity of the principal, corporate dissolution by merger, etc., to avoid unexpected invalidations and allow urgent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special authority required for certain acts (limits of general POA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative (except a patent administrator of an overseas resident) cannot perform certain acts unless given special authority: converting/abandonment/withdrawal of an application, abandonment of a patent right, withdrawal of a patent application, withdrawal of request or Domestic Priority under Article 55(1), petition for trial or designation of subagent under Article 132(3), and related special acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wording ‘all matters regarding the application’ does not include these special authorities by default. The special authority must be expressly stated (examples shown for priority claims and prior application identification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special authority examples for domestic/priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When granting authority related to priority claims, special authority must be stated in power of attorney forms (examples provided showing annotation '(Special authority related to priority claim)' and specifying application numbers/dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If special authority for priority claims is not included, representative cannot make or withdraw priority claims on behalf of principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'patent-related proceeding' (scope includes post-registration acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent-related proceeding refers to application, request and other proceedings including those after registration of a patent right; for utility model registration it also includes proceedings regarding technical evaluation after registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If representative has authority regarding matters related to technical evaluation at time of submitting application, the agent can represent matters regarding subsequent requests for technical evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent administrator rules for residents vs overseas residents
rubrics_metrics.description: A person domiciled or with place of business in the Republic of Korea can carry out patent-related proceedings without appointing an agent; an overseas resident cannot carry out patent-related proceedings or sue against administrative decisions unless sojourning in Korea, with limited exceptions (international applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international patent applications, overseas resident may carry out certain proceedings (e.g., submission of translation) without an agent but must appoint an agent within two months from the reference date and notify the Commissioner, otherwise the international application is deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling when overseas resident acts without agent
rubrics_metrics.description: If an overseas resident carries out proceedings without a patent administrator, an examiner shall give the overseas resident an opportunity to explain within a designated period; failure may lead to returning documents and addressing deficiencies via amendments (such as appointing a patent administrator) is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent administrator ceases to exist (death, revocation), examiner must contact principal to urge appointment; documents may be delivered to principal by registered airmail with warning notes about delivery and need to appoint new administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint filings: resident + overseas resident representation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application is jointly filed by a resident and an overseas resident, a resident may solely carry out proceedings except those in Article 11(1), whereas an overseas resident cannot proceed alone without appointing a patent administrator; for proceedings in Article 11(1), a resident must jointly carry out proceedings with a patent administrator appointed by the overseas resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies limitations on who may act when co-applicants include an overseas resident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent administrator authority limits for overseas residents
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent administrator of an overseas resident can represent the principal in all patent-related proceedings or lawsuits within scope of power, but cannot withdraw a patent application or a petition for trial unless given special authority for such procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent administrator's powers are subject to the same special-authority limitations as other contractual representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment/notification requirements for representatives (Article 5 Enforcement Rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appointed representative shall submit a power of attorney and a notification of appointment of a representative to prove appointment; a notification of revocation or change must be submitted to revoke/change the appointed representative. Procedures are specified in Article 5 of the Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appointment/change occurs while performing proceedings (e.g., filing an application), notification and attached power of attorney must be submitted; for intermediate proceedings only, power is limited to that intermediate proceeding unless separate notification filed to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney shall include the indication of the case for representation, the names and addresses of representative and principal, authorities empowered, and the date of preparing the power of attorney, and be signed or sealed by the principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If power of attorney content does not match submitted documents or deficiencies exist in notification/POA/subagent notification or revocation, examiner will order amendment and may invalidate proceedings if deficiencies not addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidential documents and verification of authority; consequences of deficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority of a representative must be proved in writing; absence of evidential documents, incorrect principal name, or mismatched seal is deemed representation by agent without authority. Examiner shall request amendment and require correct power of attorney; if not ratified, examiner shall invalidate the patent-related proceeding conducted by the representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment and correct POA are submitted, the power is deemed ratified by the principal and proceedings may stand.

rubrics_metrics.name: General power of attorney (GPOA) registration system
rubrics_metrics.description: The general power of attorney system grants power for all current and future cases without specifying each case; when registered, evidential documents must be attached to request for registration and submitted to the Commissioner, who grants a registration number that must be stated in documents submitted to KIPO or IPTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person may request restriction of reliance or withdrawal of registration; revocation of representative for an application filed by a rep holding registered GPOA is deemed a request for restriction for that application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement/ex officio appointment of representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Where principal or representative is recognized as unable to perform proceedings smoothly due to lack of legal capacity, the Commissioner or President of IPTAB can order the appointment of a new representative or order another representative/patent attorney to conduct proceedings ex officio to protect the principal’s interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a patent attorney is designated but lacks capacity (health/incapacity), they are deemed incapable and replacement may be ordered regardless of formal requirements under Article 10 of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of proceedings when replacement ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner or President can invalidate proceedings conducted by principal or representative before the order for appointment/replacement or before actual appointment/replacement is carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects procedural integrity where capacity issues are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-agency: right, limits, and evidential proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub-agency is representation authorized to another person by a representative; the right to appoint a subagent is granted based on principal approval or legal provisions. A legal representative generally has the right to appoint a subagent; contractual representatives or patent administrators may not appoint subagents unless granted special power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When subagent is appointed based on authority, evidential documents proving principal granted authority to appoint subagent and proving appointment by agent must be submitted (commonly the POA indicating 'Matters for Delegation').

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility/liability for acts of subagents
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal representative is responsible for all acts of his/her subagent regardless of appointment/supervision mistakes (except unavoidable reasons). A contractual representative is liable for damages to the principal only when negligent in appointment or supervision; if subagent was designated by principal, representative liable only when they knew subagent was unfit and failed to notify or revoke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different standards for legal vs contractual representatives; principal retains right to revoke subagent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and delegation limits for subagents
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of authority exercised by a subagent cannot exceed the representative's authority. If representative has authority to appoint subagent and special power from principal, representative can grant special power to subagent. In principle a subagent cannot appoint a further subagent unless principal explicitly authorized such delegation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subagent represents the principal within their authority and holds the same rights and duties as the agent with respect to principal and third parties; principal may revoke subagent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survival and extinguishment rules for subagent authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority of a subagent to conduct patent-related proceedings shall not be extinguished upon the death or loss of legal capacity of the principal, extinction of a juristic person due to merger, termination of duty of trust, death or loss of legal capacity of legal representative, or modification/extinction of representative's authority; however, subagent authority shall be extinguished for lapse causes under Civil Act or by appointment/removal of representative or subagent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This differs from general Civil Act practice to promote swift execution of proceedings; Civil Procedure Act provisions apply mutatis mutandis except special Patent Act provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple representatives and common representative rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple attorneys/representatives exist, each of them shall independently represent the principal before KIPO/IPTAB; an agreement to the contrary is not effective. If multiple representatives submit separate amendments, all are deemed legitimately submitted. When multiple parties appoint a common representative and notify KIPO, only the common representative can conduct a patent-related proceeding; more than two common representatives can be appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common representatives still need special powers to conduct proceedings under Article 11(1); otherwise examiner will request amendment and may invalidate proceedings if deficiencies are not corrected. Examiner confirms specification to be examined per the confirmation method in Part 5, Chapter 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive effect of ratified proceedings by incompetent or unauthorized persons (Article 7(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent-related proceeding conducted by a person who lacks legal capacity, power of legal representation, or necessary authorization shall have retroactive effect to the time of performance if the proceedings are ratified by the principal when he/she gains legal capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a principal who was a minor when the proceeding was initially performed but later reaches 19 (legal capacity) can ratify and give retroactive effect to the earlier proceeding.
